source.title: Weber's Law in Transformer Magnitude Representations: Efficient Coding, Representational Geometry, and Psychophysical Laws in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study discusses representational convergence across model families, but measures each model's magnitude geometry against theoretical distance structures. It does not measure pairwise alignment between models or whether such alignment rises with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The geometry results are relevant to a neighboring question—whether different models show a common log-compressive magnitude geometry—and are recorded as findings for none of the listed versions. The study does not measure cross-model representational alignment, a scale trend, shared features, or mappings between models. Behavioral and causal results concern magnitude competence, not the claim's convergence measures.
record.test_reason: The study fits each model's hidden-state distances for magnitudes against theoretical linear, log and power distance matrices. It never compares models' representations with each other and has no scale or capability sweep, seed comparison, cross-model mapping or shared-feature analysis. Its 'functional convergence' framing means each model separately shows a similar log-compressive geometry, which is a neighbouring question rather than a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that all tested models share log-compressive magnitude distance geometry (β≈0.01), acquired in pretraining, while behavioural use is model- and domain-specific and set by instruction-tuned readout. They state that the training-data-statistics explanation is correlational.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses within-model RSA and geometric model comparison against theoretical magnitude distance matrices; it does not apply a cross-model alignment method.
record.method_sensitivity: Cosine and Euclidean metrics gave identical primary-layer pass rates. The study also reports geometry across numerical, temporal, and spatial domains, but does not test whether these choices alter cross-model alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Llama, Mistral and Qwen instruct models and base Llama each show log-compressive magnitude distance structure (Stevens β≈0.01; Weber preferred over linear at all primary layers on both metrics). Qwen's fit was weaker (ρ up to .79 vs .93–.96).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained LLM families each develop a similar log-compressive geometry for magnitudes when compared against a common theoretical target, without any direct inter-model alignment being measured.

fits_no_version.finding: Despite similar geometry, behavioural readout diverges across models: Llama WF=0.20, Qwen WF=0.18, Mistral at position bias on symbolic comparison. Causal patching is effective at early layers but not at the late layers where geometry is strongest.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared representational geometry across models does not imply shared functional use of that geometry.

record.problems: No direct inter-model alignment or scale sweep is reported, so the study cannot establish the catalog claim's central trend. All models are 7–9B decoder-only models. The authors state that the data-statistics explanation is correlational and that the training distribution was not manipulated.

untested.parts: No pairwise cross-model alignment measure; all models are 7–9B, so there is no size or capability trend.
No vision models or paired image–caption data.
No linear map, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired alignment between models.
No neuron, SAE-feature or circuit matching across models; RSA is basis-agnostic, as the authors note.
Cosine and Euclidean distances agree on within-model geometry, but no test of whether metric or input choice changes cross-model alignment.
No cross-model alignment level or plateau is measured. The data-statistics explanation is offered only correlationally, for within-model geometry.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to no version. The study's 'convergence' language refers to each model separately matching a theoretical Weber RDM, not to models matching each other. A researcher might read this as indirect evidence of shared structure (a V1/V5-adjacent idea), but no inter-model similarity number is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No cross-model alignment measure or sweep over model size or capability.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language alignment.
No comparison across random seeds or analysis of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment experiment.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.
Cosine and Euclidean distances and multiple magnitude domains are used to measure within-model geometry, but the study does not test whether a measure or input choice changes cross-model convergence.
No direct measurement of cross-model alignment, its completeness or plateau, or a causal comparison of shared-data/objective explanations against a common-reality explanation.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared within-model numerical magnitude distances with linear and Weber/log geometric models using cosine distance.
rows.measure: Layers passing the stated log-over-linear criterion
rows.uncertainty: Mantel permutation tests p < .001 at all primary layers
rows.note: The criterion combines Weber RSA ρ > Linear RSA ρ and Weber AIC < Linear AIC. At peak layers, Weber R2 = .83–.88 and RSA ρ = .93–.96, versus Linear R2 = .14–.32 and RSA ρ = .51–.69. This is within-model geometry, not inter-model alignment.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared within-model numerical magnitude geometry with linear and logarithmic models using RSA and distance-model fitting.
rows.measure: Preference for logarithmic over linear geometry across primary layers
rows.value: Logarithmic preferred at every primary layer on both metrics; Weber R2 up to .54 and RSA ρ up to .79
rows.note: The text separately reports layer 28 values of .73 and .89, described as likely final-layer artifacts. It does not report pairwise alignment with the other models.

rows.subject: Llama-3-8B (base, non-instruct)
rows.operation_detail: Compared its numerical magnitude geometry with that of Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
rows.note: This is a comparison of each checkpoint's fit to theoretical numerical geometry, not a direct base–instruct alignment measure.
